divisions.name: Primary
divisions.summary: Arithmetic confidence, visual patterns and the first habits of structured reasoning.

divisions.name: Junior
divisions.summary: Algebra, triangle and circle geometry, counting and the move into written proof.

divisions.name: Secondary
divisions.summary: Olympiad geometry, number theory, functional equations and competition-level proof.

tiers.name: Gamma
tiers.summary: Build the tools: fluency, careful reading and a first repertoire of methods.
tiers.detail: Gamma is for students who need a secure base before contest work. The emphasis is on accuracy, speed and explaining a method in order.

tiers.name: Alpha
tiers.summary: Apply the tools to regional and national problem styles.
tiers.detail: Alpha assumes working fluency. Problems are longer, often combine two ideas, and require a written argument rather than an answer alone.

tiers.name: Sigma
tiers.summary: Train at the top of the national and international range.
tiers.detail: Sigma is the advanced tier: multi-step proofs, unfamiliar configurations and international-style papers. Placement is reviewed every month.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Number intuition, arithmetic speed, visual patterns and logic puzzles.

sample.hint: Pair the first and last terms, then count how many pairs there are.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Contest arithmetic, divisibility, counting, pigeonhole and multi-step problems.

sample.q: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add to 9?
sample.hint: The tens digit can be 1 through 9. For each choice, the units digit is fixed.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: BdMO primary-level problem sets, IMSO-style questions and first proofs.

sample.q: A square is cut into four equal smaller squares. If the original perimeter is 24 cm, what is the perimeter of one small square?
sample.hint: Find the side of the original square first, then halve it.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Foundational algebra, triangle geometry and the first habits of proof writing.
syllabus: Writing a proof in clear steps

sample.hint: Expand the left side, then collect the x-terms.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Regional and national BdMO styles: counting, invariants, modular arithmetic and prime factorisation.

sample.q: Find the remainder when 3¹⁰⁰ is divided by 7.
sample.hint: The powers of 3 modulo 7 repeat every six steps.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Circle geometry, cyclic quadrilaterals, functional equations and inequalities.

sample.q: Two chords of a circle intersect inside the circle. One chord is split into 4 cm and 6 cm. The other is split into 3 cm and x cm. Find x.

mathBatches.subject: Mathematics
mathBatches.summary: Inversive and projective geometry, Diophantine equations and polynomials.

sample.q: Find all positive integers n such that n² + 1 is divisible by n + 1.

scienceBatches.subject: Science
scienceBatches.summary: Integrated primary science with circuits, optics, mixtures, reactions, classification and ecosystems.

sample.q: A cell, a switch and a bulb are connected in one series loop. What happens when the bulb fails?
sample.hint: A series circuit has only one path for the current.
sample.answer: The circuit is broken, so no current flows and the other components stop working.

scienceBatches.subject: Science
scienceBatches.summary: Motion, forces, atomic structure, bonding, cell anatomy and titration technique.
syllabus: Atomic structure and the periodic table

sample.q: A car travels 100 m in 20 s. What is its average speed?
sample.hint: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

scienceBatches.subject: Science
scienceBatches.summary: IJSO preparation: calculus-based mechanics, optics, thermodynamics, stoichiometry, equilibrium, genetics and error analysis.

sample.q: A 2 kg block is pushed across a frictionless floor by a 10 N horizontal force. What is its acceleration?
sample.hint: Use Newton’s second law: F = ma.

placement.heading: How placement works
placement.summary: A diagnostic test, a written placement, then a monthly review. Class in school does not decide the tier.

steps.title: Diagnostic test
steps.description: The student sits a short written diagnostic. It is a placement test, not a pass/fail entrance exam.

steps.title: Ability, not grade
steps.description: The result places the student in a division and tier. A strong Class 6 student can sit in a Junior Sigma batch; a Class 9 student may start in a foundation group.

steps.title: Written confirmation
steps.description: The batch, session and fee are confirmed in writing before the first class.

steps.title: Monthly benchmark
steps.description: Weekly problem sets build to a monthly benchmark. The top quartile may move up; a student who is slipping is re-placed.

reviews: Weekly problem sets are marked and returned with feedback.
A monthly benchmark checks whether the current tier still fits.
The top quartile of a batch may be promoted at the review.
A student who is slipping is re-placed rather than left behind.
Acceleration can happen at any time, not only at the monthly review.

promotion.heading: The promotion path
promotion.summary: Gamma builds the tools, Alpha applies them, Sigma stretches them. Movement is evidence-led and can happen in either direction.
rules: Promotion is based on the monthly benchmark, not on time served.
The top quartile of a batch may move up at the monthly review.
A student who is slipping is re-placed into a group where the work fits.
Acceleration is available at any point when the evidence supports it.
The monthly fee stays the same after promotion.
